issues.quote: | A16 | Ava sets an appointment | Before open | Time on the handoff; BDC manager keys it in, cancels any prior duplicate, calls to confirm; CSM checks week one | R5 happy [E6, E12] (Q32) |
issues.concern: The only way an Ava-set appointment reaches my board is one person keying it in before open, and after week one nobody checks that she did. My BDC manager has days off, and Saturday night leads land on a Sunday when the BDC may be closed. The email goes to her alone ("Email recipient: BDC manager"). On the day she is out, a customer Ava booked for 9 am walks in and nobody expects them. That is the empty-bay day in my own seat description, and the PRD has no detection for it after week one.
issues.because: E12, E13 (no API, keying is the only path); persona Blocks when: customer-facing failure with no detection or recovery path; persona Review lens: Adoption cost (works without manager enforcement)
issues.ask: Name a backup recipient for the handoff (desk manager or BDC lead) and send the email to both. State what happens to an Ava-set appointment for a day or hour the BDC is closed. Keep a weekly CSM check that every Ava-set appointment was on the board before its time for as long as step 0 runs, not just in week one. Add one acceptance row: on the BDC manager's day off, an Ava-set appointment still reaches the board before its time.

issues.quote: | A17 | Email lacks R5's fields | Go-live review | Go only with the VP Marketing's written acceptance of Console; BDC manager then works the Console list | R5 fallback [E13] |
issues.concern: The fallback hands R5 to Console, but nothing shows that the Console list carries R5's fields either: appointment date and time, "callback requested" with the customer's words (R12), and not-texted with reason. Q35 asks where an after-hours transfer routes, not where the request shows up. If neither the email nor Console shows that a customer asked for a person at 11 pm, my BDC does not call that customer first and A14 cannot pass. The VP Marketing would be signing off a screen that does not do the job.
issues.because: Q26 (email untraced); Q35 (routing only); section 5 'BDC handoff ... not traced'; persona Blocks when: asks staff to check a separate dashboard to know what happened
issues.ask: Add to the Q26 go-live check: whichever surface is chosen (email or Console) is shown with a UAT lead to carry appointment date and time and a callback-requested flag with the customer's words, and A14 and A16 are run on that surface. If neither surface carries them, no go-live, the same as A3.

issues.quote: | R10 | The CSM reconciles forwarded leads against STL tasks (noTask apart) and checks non-inquiry texts daily in week one, then weekly while step 0 runs; follow-up rows are checked daily throughout | P0 | [PM] [E41] |
issues.concern: R4 says a non-STOP opt-out is "found in the daily check" and optOut.sms is set the same morning. R10 never names an opt-out check, and the checks it does name go weekly after week one. So from week two, a customer who wrote "unsubscribe" can be re-forwarded after the 15-hour window and get a text from my store's number. That is the store's liability, and the GM or dealer principal is the one signing Q24.
issues.because: E42 (exact STOP only); A7 (15-hour suppression only); A12; Q37
issues.ask: Name the non-STOP opt-out scan in R10 and keep it daily for as long as step 0 runs, the same as the follow-up rows. Alternatively, make the handoff's 'opted out' status the trigger: the BDC manager sends each opted-out row to the CSM that morning and ops sets optOut.sms. Add the case to A12: an unsubscribe in week three is still set the next morning.

issues.quote: - **Dealer message (CSM):** "Inquiries go live N business days after your after-hours texts are paused and the test leads pass. Whether appointment and credit-app texts can be built is answered by <step 1 date>. Write-back is planned, and we date it once the channel is agreed." Step 2 pilot order stays internal.
issues.concern: This store has already chased us with unanswered ETA requests (E10, E31). If the CSM sends this before the Q34 path test and the test shows the queue path, step 0 is a no-go with no date, and we have broken a second promise. The message also tells the dealer to pause their own after-hours texts, which leaves their leads untouched overnight if we then cannot go live.
issues.because: E10, E31; Q34; A6; decisions.md Gate 2 ('queue path may skip it'); persona What they protect: vendor trust
issues.ask: The CSM sends this message only after the Q34 test shows the API path, and the dealer pauses its texts only after that. Write the second message for the queue-path outcome: step 0 cannot go live on configuration, the BDC keeps working as today, and the next answer comes by the date the PM sets under E-1.

issues.concern: A5 and the staleness edge case expect some leads to be skipped: outside the window, or forwarded more than 6 hours late. A target of 0 fails every week by design, so my BDC manager learns to ignore it. This was supposed to be the week-one skip count the VP Marketing needs to see what skipped leads cost (gm-r1-4).
issues.ask: Split the row. `sqs-stl-deferred-to-api` stays at target 0, since it means a no-go. Outside-window and stale skips are counted weekly by reason and shown on the handoff, with no target, and the week-one count goes to the VP Marketing alongside the Q25 acceptance.

issues.quote: | A13 | Dealer pause unconfirmed | Go-live review | No go-live | R4 fallback [E15, E43] |
issues.concern: Section 4 allows go-live with no pause if the VP Marketing accepts in writing that skipped leads get no overnight touch. A13 says no go-live without the pause, full stop. The dealer's system may not be able to pause only for leads Spyne texts, so the CSM will hit this conflict on the first go-live review.
